il_d_lovely_tower.blurb: Lovely Tower is a detached, freestanding block of sandstone in the North Falls stretch of the Jackson Falls canyon in southern Illinois, reached by walking the cliff line past a large roof. Fourteen climbs cover mostly bolted sport lines, with two trad routes and two top-ropes. The grades skew hard: a few lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, then a cluster around 5.12 with some 5.11 and 5.13, and one at the 5.14 level. It suits climbers working at 5.11 and up, and it sits in a part of the canyon with plenty of neighboring walls to combine in one day.

il_c_cranial_detox_wall.blurb: Cranial/Detox Wall is a sizeable sandstone cliff in the Hidden Peaks section of Jackson Falls, Illinois, running alongside a pair of large separated towers. Of its fourteen climbs, twelve are sport and two are trad. This is a hard-climber's wall: ten of the lines fall in the 5.12 range, two are 5.11, and only a couple are easier, so it rewards people already comfortable on steep, bolted sandstone. Reaching it takes a short canyon-rim walk and a second-class scramble down, which keeps the total approach modest compared with the far reaches of the canyon.

il_h_hobo_cave.blurb: Hobo Cave is a shaded, roofed sandstone alcove in the North Canyon zone of Jackson Falls, southern Illinois, found on the way toward Railroad Rock beyond a couple of other walls. Fourteen routes include ten sport lines, three trad and a single aid line. The difficulty is mostly in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with a few easier outings near 5.7 and 5.8 and a couple of 5.13 lines at the top end. The overhanging, cave-like character and shade make it a reasonable refuge on warm days for climbers who like steep, powerful movement.

il_e_exam_wall.blurb: Exam Wall is a popular sandstone wall in the West Falls part of Jackson Falls, Illinois, a short stroll south of the waterfall along the trail beneath the cliff. The face starts out southwest-facing with a wide crack on its right, then turns into a corridor beside a detached tower. Fourteen climbs split between nine sport and five trad routes. Grades run from a few 5.9 and 5.10 lines through a steady diet of 5.11 and 5.12, finishing with a few 5.13s, so it is best for confident leaders who want crack and face climbing side by side.

il_b_the_ampitheater.blurb: The Ampitheater is a big, overhanging bowl of sandstone in Giant City State Park near Carbondale, Illinois, just left of the Devils Standtable formation. To get there, take the main trail from the parking, stay right along the bluff, then descend. The fourteen climbs here are mostly bolted sport lines with two trad routes, and the style feels different from the rest of the park. Grades start around 5.6 and 5.7, bunch up in the 5.13 range, and top out near 5.14. Many first bolts are high, so bring a stick clip.

il_e_dawg_pound_boulder.blurb: Dawg Pound Boulder is a large block sitting in a sinkhole just uphill from another boulder in the House Boulders, on the western edge of Shawnee National Forest in southern Illinois. The fine-grained sandstone here is stacked on a steep, wooded, west-facing hillside. All fourteen problems are bouldering, covering slabs, faces and a tall center line. Grades spread from VB-level easy lines up to V7, with most problems in the V2 to V4 range, so there is something for beginners and for strong boulderers. Some of the taller lines are serious if you fall.

il_a_playground_wall_detention_area.blurb: Playground Wall is the first cliff you meet after the walk up an old road at Cedar Bluff in southern Illinois, part of a half-mile band of 80 to 90 foot sandstone cliffs. Fourteen climbs split between eight trad and six sport routes, and several are two pitches, which makes it a handy place to practice multi-pitch systems. Grades begin near 5.5 and 5.6, build through 5.8 to 5.10, with a handful at 5.12. It is a good pick for a mixed-ability party that wants both moderate trad and harder bolted lines.
